name: Accountants and Associates
tasks: Accountants plan, organize and administer accounting systems for individuals and establishments. They also examine and analyze the accounting and financial records of individuals and establishments to ensure accuracy and compliance with established accounting standards and procedures. Accounting associates maintain complete records of financial transactions of an undertaking and verify accuracy of documents and records relating to such transactions.

name: Advertising and Marketing Professionals
tasks: Advertising and marketing professionals develop and coordinate advertising strategies and campaigns, determine the market for new goods and services, and identify and develop market opportunities for new and existing goods and services.

name: Case Officials
tasks: Case officials handles and investigate cases and complaints submitted regarding the services provided by the organization.

name: Compliance and Regulation Inspectors
tasks: Compliance and regulation inspectors monitors work environments to ensure they meets government regulations.

name: Conference and Events Planners
tasks: Conference and events planners organize and coordinate services for conferences, events, functions, banquets and seminars.

name: Finance Managers
tasks: Finance managers plan, direct and coordinate the financial operations of the organization, in consultation with senior managers and with managers of other departments or sections.

name: Financial Analysts
tasks: Financial analysts conduct quantitative analyses of information affecting finances and investment programmes of public or private institutions.

name: Financial, Business and Investment Strategists
tasks: Develop financial, business and investment plans for individuals and organizations, and invest, manage and strategize funds on their behalf.

name: Government Licensing Officials
tasks: Government licensing officials examine applications for licences to export or import goods, set up businesses, build houses or other structures, determine eligibility of applications for issuing licences, and identify specific conditions or restrictions to be attached to licences issued, referring exceptional or important cases to senior government officials or managers.

name: Government Social Benefits Officials
tasks: Government social benefits officials examine applications for government, financial or service programmes to determine eligibility and amount of benefit or appropriate services.

name: Human Capital Professionals
tasks: Human capital professionals guide the organization through human resource procedures and are involved in setting and reviewing compensation and benefits, and employee relations issues.

name: Human Resource Managers
tasks: Human resource managers plan, direct and coordinate policies concerning the human resource management, industrial relations and occupational health and safety activities of the organization.

name: Human Resources, Administrative & Executive Secretaries
tasks: Human resources, administrative and executive secretaries provide human resources, organizational, communication and documentation support services, utilizing specialized knowledge of the business activity of the organization in which they are employed.

name: Management and Organization Analysts
tasks: Management and organization analysts assist organizations to achieve greater efficiency and solve organizational problems. They study organizational structures, methods, systems and procedures.

name: Policy Administration Professionals
tasks: Policy administration professionals develop and analyze policies guiding the design, implementation and modification of government and commercial operations and programmes.

name: Policy and Planning Managers
tasks: Policy and planning managers plan, organize, direct and coordinate policy advice and strategic planning activities within government or for services provided by the government for non-government organizations and private sector agencies.

name: Procurement Professionals and Tenderers
tasks: Procurement professionals plan, direct and coordinate procurement policies, processes and procedures either as the manager of a department or as the general manager of an organization that does not have a hierarchy of managers. Tenderers buy goods and services for use or resale on behalf of industrial, commercial, government or other establishments and organizations.

name: Project & Program Management Professionals and Associates
tasks: Project management professionals are responsible for coordinating and completing projects on time within the allocated budget and within the scope of the project. They oversee all aspects of the project that include setting deadlines, assigning responsibilities and monitoring and summarizing the progress of the project.
titles: E m e r g e n c y R e s p o n s e Associate

name: Public Debt Professionals
tasks: Public debt professionals are responsible for setting and managing the policy on sovereign debt.

name: Public Funds Management Professionals
tasks: Public funds management professionals are responsible for managing, mobilizing and disbursement of public funds and resources.
titles: Public Funds Manager. Public Funds Analyst

name: Public Relations Professionals
tasks: Public relations professionals plan, develop, implement and evaluate information and communication strategies that create an understanding and a favourable view of businesses and other organizations, their goods and services, and their role in the community.

name: Research and Development Managers
tasks: Research and development managers plan, direct and coordinate the research and development activities of organizations.

name: Tax and Revenue Collectors
tasks: Tax and revenue collectors examine tax returns, bills of sale and other documents to determine the type and amount of taxes, duties and other types of fees to be paid by individuals or businesses.

name: Training and Staff Development Professionals
tasks: Training and staff development professionals plan, develop, implement and evaluate training and development programmes to ensure management and staff acquire the skills and develop the competencies required by organizations to meet organizational objectives.

name: Audiologists and Speech Therapists
tasks: Audiologists and speech therapists evaluate, manage and treat physical disorders affecting human hearing, speech, and communication and swallowing. They prescribe corrective devices or rehabilitative therapies for hearing loss, speech disorders and related sensory and neural problems, and provide counselling on hearing safety and communication performance.

name: Biomedical Engineers
tasks: Biomedical engineer analyzes and designs solutions to problems in biology and medicine, with the goal of improving the quality and effectiveness of patient care.

name: Dentists and Dental Technician
tasks: Dentists diagnose, treat and prevent diseases, injuries and abnormalities of the teeth, mouth, jaws and associated tissues by applying the principles and procedures of modern dentistry. Dental technicians design, fit, service and repair medical and dental devices and appliances following prescriptions or instructions established by a health professional.

name: Dieticians and Nutritionists
tasks: Dieticians and nutritionists assess, plan and implement programmes to enhance the impact of food and nutrition on human health.

name: Environmental, Health and Occupational Health Professionals and Associates
tasks: Environmental, health and occupational health inspectors and associates investigate the implementation of rules and regulations relating to environmental and health factors that may affect human health, safety in the workplace, and safety of processes for the production of goods and services. They may implement and evaluate programmes to restore or improve safety and sanitary conditions under the supervision of a health professional.

name: Generalist and Specialist Medical Doctors
tasks: Generalist medical practitioners (including family and primary care doctors) diagnose, treat and prevent illness, disease, injury and other physical and mental impairments and maintain general health in humans through application of the principles and procedures of modern medicine. They do not limit their practice to certain disease categories or methods of treatment, and may assume responsibility for the provision of continuing and comprehensive medical care to individuals, families and communities. Specialist medical practitioners (medical doctors) diagnose, treat and prevent illness, disease, injury and other physical and mental impairments in humans, using specialized testing, diagnostic, medical, surgical, physical and psychiatric techniques through application of the principles and procedures of modern medicine. They specialize in certain disease categories, types of patient or methods of treatment and may conduct medical education and research in their chosen areas of specialization.

name: Health Services Managers
tasks: Health services managers plan, direct, coordinate and evaluate the provision of clinical and community health care services in hospitals, clinics, public health agencies and similar organizations.

name: Medical and Health Care Assistants
tasks: Medical assistants perform basic clinical and administrative tasks to support patient care under the direct supervision of a medical practitioner or other health professional. Health care assistants provide direct personal care and assistance with activities of daily living to patients and residents in a variety of health care settings such as hospitals, clinics and residential nursing care facilities.

name: Medical Imaging and Therapeutic Equipment Technicians
tasks: Medical imaging and therapeutic equipment technicians test and operate radiographic, ultrasound and other medical imaging equipment to produce images of body structures for the diagnosis and treatment of injury, disease and other impairments. They may administer radiation treatments to patients under the supervision of a radiologist or other health professional.

name: Medical, Pathology and Public Health Laboratory Technicians
tasks: Medical and pathology laboratory technicians perform clinical tests on specimens of bodily fluids and tissues in order to obtain information about the health of a patient or cause of death. Public health laboratory technicians focuses on diagnostic testing and disease surveillance for public health purposes.

name: Medical Records and Health Information Technicians
tasks: Medical records and health information technicians develop, maintain and implement health records processing, storage and retrieval systems in medical facilities and other health care settings to meet the legal, professional, ethical and administrative record-keeping requirements of health services delivery.
titles: Medical Records and Health Information Analyst
Medical Records and Health Information Technician

name: Nursing and Midwifery Professionals and Associates
tasks: Nursing professionals provide treatment, support and care services for people who are in need of nursing care due to the effects of ageing, injury, illness or other physical or mental impairment, or potential risks to health. Midwifery professionals plan, manage, provide and evaluate midwifery care services before, during and after pregnancy and childbirth.

name: Optometrists and Ophthalmic Opticians
tasks: Optometrists and ophthalmic opticians provide diagnosis, management and treatment services for disorders of the eyes and visual system. They counsel on eye care and prescribe optical aids or other therapies for visual disturbance.

name: Paramedical Practitioners and Emergency Medical Technicians
tasks: Paramedical practitioners provide advisory, diagnostic, curative and preventive medical services more limited in scope and complexity than those carried out by medical doctors. Emergency medical technicians provide emergency health care to patients who are injured, sick, infirm or otherwise physically or mentally impaired prior to and during transport to medical facilities.

name: Pharmacists and Pharmaceutical Technicians
tasks: Pharmacists store, preserve, compound and dispense medicinal products and counsel on the proper use and adverse effects of drugs and medicines following prescriptions issued by medical doctors and other health professionals. Pharmaceutical technicians perform a variety of tasks associated with dispensing medicinal products under the guidance of a pharmacist or other health professional.

name: Physiotherapists, Occupational Therapists and Technicians
tasks: Physiotherapist rehabilitates patients by helping them improve their physical movement. They treat people who are injured or disabled in order to recover full function and movement. It's both cure and prevention focused, and requires in-depth anatomical and musculoskeletal knowledge. Occupational therapists treat injured, ill, or disabled patients through the therapeutic use of everyday activities. They help these patients develop, recover, improve, as well as maintain the skills needed for daily living and working.

name: Public Health Professionals and Associates
tasks: Public health professionals undertake research on community health issues, educate and promote healthy lifestyles in communities, and establish health standards and programs both as a preventive mechanism as well as health crisis management.

name: Traditional and Complementary Medicine Professionals
tasks: Traditional and complementary medicine professionals examine patients, prevent and treat illness, disease, injury and other physical and mental impairments and maintain general health in humans by applying knowledge, skills and practices acquired through extensive study of the theories, beliefs and experiences, originating in specific cultures.

name: Veterinarians and Veterinary Technicians
tasks: Veterinarians diagnose, prevent and treat diseases, injuries and dysfunctions of animals. Veterinary technicians and assistants carry out advisory, diagnostic, preventive and curative veterinary tasks, more limited in scope and complexity than those carried out by, and with the guidance of, veterinarians.

name: Database and Network Professionals
tasks: Database and network professionals design, develop, control, maintain and support the optimal performance and security of information technology systems and infrastructure, including databases, hardware and software, networks and operating systems.

name: Information and Communications Technology Operations and User Support Technicians
tasks: Information technology operations and user support technicians provide support for the day-to-day running of communications systems, computer systems and networks, and provide technical assistance to users.

name: Information and Communications Technology Services Managers
tasks: Information and communications technology services managers plan, direct and coordinate the acquisition, development, maintenance and use of computer and telecommunication systems.

name: Software and Applications Developers and Analysts
tasks: Software and applications developers and analysts conduct research; plan, design, write, test, provide advice on and improve information technology systems such as hardware, software and other applications to meet specific requirements.

name: Archivists and Curators
tasks: Archivists and curators collect, appraise and ensure the safekeeping and preservation of the contents of archives, artefacts and records of historical, cultural, administrative and artistic interest, and of art and other objects.

name: Authors, Journalists and Linguists
tasks: Authors, journalists and linguists conceive and create literary works; interpret and communicate news and public affairs through the media; and translate or interpret from one language into another.

name: Community Empowerment and Engagement Professionals
tasks: Community empowerment and engagement professionals engage in activities and processes which is intended to benefit organizations and individuals in a community thereby building an ongoing and permanent relationship for the purpose of applying a collective vision for the benefit of the community.

name: Counsellors, Social Workers, and Associates
tasks: Counsellors and social workers provide advice and guidance to individuals, families, groups, communities and organizations in response to social and personal difficulties. Social work associates administer and implement social assistance programmes and community services and assist clients to deal with personal and social problems.

name: Creative and Performing Artists
tasks: Creative and performing artists communicate ideas, impressions and facts in a wide range of media to achieve particular effects; interpret a composition such as a musical score or a script to perform or direct the performance; and host the presentation of such performance and other media events.

name: Diplomats and Diplomatic Secretaries
tasks: Diplomats represent and protect the interests and nationals of the sending state; initiate and facilitate strategic agreements, treaties and conventions; promote trade, commerce, technology and friendly relations. Diplomatic secretaries, using specific knowledge of diplomatic and consular corps, assist diplomats, consular professionals and other workers by performing a variety of communication, documentation, administrative and internal coordination functions.

name: Economists and Associates
tasks: Economist conduct research, monitor data, analyze information and prepare reports and plans to resolve economic and business problems and develop models to analyze, explain and forecast economic behaviour and patterns. Economic Associates are responsible for continuously developing and maintaining knowledge required to do the job by understanding, embracing and contributing to the community’s economic development.

name: Fitness and Recreation Instructors and Programme Leaders
tasks: Fitness and recreation instructors and programme leaders lead, guide and instruct groups and individuals in recreational, fitness or outdoor adventure activities.

name: Legal Professionals and Associates
tasks: Lawyers give clients legal advice on a wide variety of subjects, draw up legal documents, represent clients before administrative boards or tribunals and plead cases or conduct prosecutions in courts of justice, or instruct barristers to plead in higher courts of justice. Legal associates apply specialized knowledge of legal terminology and procedures in providing support to legal professionals with communication, documentation and internal managerial coordination activities, in law offices, legal departments of large firms and governments.

name: Librarians and Associates
tasks: Librarians collect, select, develop, organize and maintain library collections and other information repositories; organize and control other library services and provide information for users.

name: Religious Service Professionals and Associates
tasks: Religious professionals function as perpetuators of sacred traditions, practices and beliefs of Islam. They conduct religious services, celebrate or administer the rites of a religious faith or denomination, provide spiritual and moral guidance and perform other functions associated with the practice of Islam. Religious associates provide support to the community, undertake religious works, preach and propagate the general teachings of Islam and endeavour to improve well-being through the power of faith and spiritual advice.

name: Social Welfare Managers
tasks: Social welfare managers plan, direct and coordinate the provision of social and community service programmes such as income support, family assistance, children’s services and other community programmes and services.

name: Sociologists and Psychologists
tasks: Sociologists investigate and describe the structure, origin and evolution of societies and the interdependence between environmental conditions and human activities. Psychologists research into and study the mental processes and behaviour of human beings as individuals or in groups, and apply this knowledge to promote personal, social, educational or occupational adjustment and development.

name: Sports Coaches, Instructors and Officials
tasks: Sports coaches, instructors and officials work with amateur and professional sportspersons to enhance performance and encourage greater participation in sport, and organize and officiate in sporting events according to established rules.

name: Transport Management Professionals and Associates
tasks: Transport management professionals are responsible for developing transportation strategies that encompass the needs of all transport users including pedestrians, motorists and cyclists, thereby considering the environmental, efficiency and safety issues.

name: Airworthiness Engineers
tasks: Airworthiness engineers ensure that aircraft are fit to fly and comply with all the relevant aviation regulations. They deal with aircraft and associated software systems that test for airworthiness on a regular basis.

name: Agricultural, Fisheries and Forestry Technicians
tasks: Agricultural technicians perform tests and experiments, and provide technical and scientific support to agricultural scientists, farmers and farm managers. Fisheries technicians perform tests and experiments, perform technical and supervisory functions in support of fisheries research and fisheries management, and provide technical and scientific support to fisheries managers and advisers. Forestry technicians perform technical and supervisory functions in support of forestry research and forest management, harvesting, resource conservation and environmental protection.
titles: P o u l t r y T e c h n i c i a n
F o r e s t r y Technician

name: Aquaculturists & Aquaculture Technicians
tasks: Aquaculturists specialize in operating, monitoring, and maintaining aquatic farms, including rearing fish classes in natural or controlled environmental such as tanks, ponds, or net cages. Aquaculture technicians breed and raise fish and cultivate mussels, oysters and other forms of aquatic life, for sale or delivery on a regular basis to wholesale buyers, marketing organizations or at markets.

name: Architectural and Building Engineers
tasks: Architectural and building engineers focus on building engineering features during the design of commercial, industrial, institutional, residential and recreational buildings. They are expected to have a functional knowledge of designing, mechanical and structural systems combined with the managing of its lightening and electrical systems.

name: Biologists, Botanists and Zoologists
tasks: Biologists, botanists and zoologists study living organisms and their interactions with each other and with the environment, and apply this knowledge to solving human health and environmental problems. They work in diverse fields such as botany, zoology, ecology, marine biology, genetics, immunology, pharmacology, toxicology, physiology, bacteriology and virology.

name: Building Architects
tasks: Building architects design commercial, industrial, institutional, residential and recreational buildings and plan and monitor their construction, maintenance and rehabilitation.

name: Cartographers and Surveyors
tasks: Cartographers and surveyors determine the exact position of, or prepare and revise digital, graphic and pictorial maps, charts or other visual representation of, natural and constructed features and boundaries of land, seas, underground areas and celestial bodies, applying scientific and mathematical principles.

name: Civil Engineers and Technicians
tasks: Civil engineers conduct research, advise on, design, and direct construction; manage the operation and maintenance of civil engineering structures; or study and advise on technological aspects of particular materials. Civil engineering technicians perform technical tasks in civil engineering research and in the design, construction, operation, maintenance and repair of buildings and other structures such as water supply and wastewater treatment systems, bridges, roads, dams and airports.

name: Draughtspersons
tasks: Draughtspersons prepare technical drawings, maps and illustrations from sketches, measurements and other data, and copy final drawings and paintings onto printing plates.

name: Electrical Engineers and Technicians
tasks: Electrical engineers conduct research and advice on, design and direct the construction and operation of electrical systems, components, motors and equipment, and advice on and direct their functioning, maintenance and repair, or study and advice on technological aspects of electrical engineering materials, products and processes. Electrical engineering technicians perform technical tasks to aid in electrical engineering research and in the design, manufacture, assembly, construction, operation, maintenance and repair of electrical equipment, facilities and distribution systems.

name: Environmental Engineers and Technicians
tasks: Environmental engineers conduct research, advice on, design and direct implementation of solutions to prevent, control or remedy negative impacts of human activity on the environment utilizing a variety of engineering disciplines. They also assist scientists and engineers engaged in developing procedures or conducting research on environmental engineering.

name: Environmental Protection Professionals and Associates
tasks: Environmental protection professionals study and assess the effects on the environment of human activity such as air, water and noise pollution, soil contamination, climate change, toxic waste and depletion and degradation of natural resources. They develop plans and solutions to protect, conserve, restore, minimize and prevent further damage to the environment.

name: Farming, Forestry and Fisheries Professionals
tasks: Farming, forestry and fisheries professionals study and provide assistance and advice on farm, forestry and fisheries management, including cultivation, fertilization, harvesting, soil erosion and composition, disease prevention, nutrition, crop rotation and marketing. They develop techniques for increasing productivity, and study and develop plans and policies for land and fisheries management.

name: Graphic and Multimedia Designers
tasks: Graphic and multimedia designers design visual and audiovisual content for the communication of information using print, film, electronic, digital and other forms of visual and audio media.

name: Interior Designers and Decorators
tasks: Interior designers and decorators plan and design commercial, industrial, public, retail and residential building interiors to produce an environment tailored to a purpose, taking into consideration factors that enhance living and working environments and sales promotion.

name: Landscape Architects
tasks: Landscape architects plan and design landscapes and open spaces for projects such as parks, schools, institutions, roads, external areas for commercial, industrial and residential sites, and plan and monitor their construction, maintenance and rehabilitation.

name: Mechanical Engineers and Technicians
tasks: Mechanical engineers conduct research; advise on, design, and direct production of machines, aircraft, ships, machinery and industrial plant, equipment and systems; advise on and direct their functioning, maintenance and repair; or study and advise on mechanical aspects of particular materials, products or processes.

name: Meteorologists
tasks: Meteorologists prepare short-term or long-term weather forecasts used in aviation, shipping, agriculture and other areas and for the information of the general public. They conduct research related to the composition, structure and dynamics of the atmosphere.

name: Quantity Surveyors and Technicians
tasks: Quantity surveyor is a construction industry professional with expert knowledge on construction costs and contracts. They manages the costs related to building and civil engineering projects, from initial projections to the final figures.

name: Statisticians and Statistical Associates
tasks: Statisticians conduct research and improve or develop statistical concepts, theories and operational methods and techniques and advise on or engage in their practical application in such fields as engineering, business and social and other sciences.

name: Educational Managers
tasks: Education managers plan, direct, coordinate and evaluate the educational and administrative aspects of education services, primary and secondary schools, colleges and faculties and departments in universities and other educational institutions.

name: Educational Planning Professionals and Associates
tasks: Educational planners develop and analyze issues, trends or policies that are affecting education. They may include cost, equality of access, new technologies, curriculum or learning and teaching methods.

name: School Teachers
tasks: School teachers comprise of pre-school, primary, secondary and higher secondary teachers of all subjects.

name: University and Higher Education Teachers
tasks: University and higher education teachers prepare and deliver lectures and conduct tutorials in one or more subjects within a prescribed course of study at a university or other higher educational institution. They conduct research, and prepare scholarly papers and books.

name: Vocational Teachers
tasks: Vocational education teachers teach or instruct vocational or occupational subjects in adult and further education institutions and to senior students in secondary schools and colleges.

name: Secretarial Support Workers
tasks: Secretarial support workers record, organize, store, compute and retrieve information, and perform a number of clerical and secretarial duties in connection with money-handling operations, travel arrangements, requests for information, appointments, and daily administrative functions.

name: Skilled Workers
tasks: Skilled workers perform labour or work that demands skills, training and knowledge that is usually acquired by attending a college or vocational training centre.

name: Elementary Workers
tasks: Elementary workers perform operations that involve the execution of simple duties, which require the experience of little or no independent judgement or previous experience, although familiarity with the occupational environment is necessary. Their work may involve the use of hand-held tools and require considerable physical effort.

name: Armed Forces Occupations
tasks: Armed forces occupations include all jobs held by members of the armed forces. Members of the armed forces are those personnel who are currently serving in the armed forces, including auxiliary services, whether on a voluntary or compulsory basis, and who are not free to accept civilian employment and are subject to military discipline. Included are regular members of the army, navy, air force and other military services, as well as conscripts enrolled for military training or other service for a specified period.

name: Police Service
tasks: Police service workers protect individuals and property against crime, maintain law and order, and enforce laws and regulations.

name: Firefighters
tasks: Firefighters prevent, fight and extinguish fires and assist in other emergencies, protect life and property and conduct rescue efforts.

name: Prison Guards
tasks: Prison guards watch over and maintain order among inmates of prisons, reformatories or penitentiaries.

name: Security Guards
tasks: Security guards patrol or monitor premises to guard property against theft and vandalism. They control access to establishments and maintain order and enforce regulations at public events and within establishments.

name: Customs and Boarder Inspectors
tasks: Customs and border inspectors check persons and vehicles crossing national borders to administer and enforce relevant government rules and regulations. ------------------------------- 04 September 2019
